Build a measurable-data summary

Source: R/api-tables.R
measurable_summary_table.Rd

Build a measurable-data summary

Usage

measurable_summary_table(fit, diagnostics = NULL)

Arguments

fit

Output from fit_mfrm().

diagnostics

Optional output from diagnose_mfrm(). Must match this fitted analysis; see mfrmr_compatibility_layer for migration of saved diagnostics.

Value

A named list with:

  • summary: one-row measurable-data summary

  • facet_coverage: per-facet coverage summary

  • category_stats: category-level usage/fit summary

  • subsets: subset summary table (when available)

Details

This helper consolidates measurable-data diagnostics into a dedicated report bundle: run-level summary, facet coverage, category usage, and subset (connected-component) information.

summary(t5) is supported through summary(). plot(t5) is dispatched through plot() for class mfrm_measurable (type = "facet_coverage", "category_counts", "subset_observations").

Interpreting output

summary describes the retained analysis; it is not a sample-size adequacy decision. LargestSubsetPct concerns rating rows, not independent Persons or the proportion of planned assignments completed. A connected design alone does not establish parameter precision or identify every model term.

facet_coverage summarizes the supplied diagnostic rows. MeanSE is the unweighted mean of available element SEs, not the SE of the facet mean or the RMS error used for separation reliability. For MML Persons these SEs are posterior SDs. Means omit missing values separately for each column; they can describe different subsets of levels. An all-missing mean is NaN, not zero error. Inspect diagnostics$measures for missing values and their reasons before comparing facets; see diagnose_mfrm().

category_stats describes observed category usage and plug-in expectations. It does not certify category adequacy. See rating_scale_table() for the meaning of expected counts, residual summaries and step offsets.

Typical workflow

  1. Run measurable_summary_table(fit).

  2. Check summary(t5) for subset/connectivity warnings.

  3. Use plot(t5, ...) to inspect facet/category/subset views.

Further guidance

For a plot-selection guide and a longer walkthrough, see mfrmr_visual_diagnostics and vignette("mfrmr-visual-diagnostics", package = "mfrmr").

Output columns

The summary data.frame (one row) contains:

Observations, TotalWeight

Retained rating-row count and summed response weight, respectively. Neither is an independent-Person count.

Persons, Facets, Categories

Retained Persons, non-Person facets and declared score categories (including unused categories).

ConnectedSubsets

Number of connected subsets.

LargestSubsetObs, LargestSubsetPct

Rows in the largest connected subset and 100 * LargestSubsetObs / Observations.

The facet_coverage data.frame contains:

Facet

Facet name.

Levels

Number of diagnostic rows, including levels with missing SEs.

MeanSE

Arithmetic mean of available element SEs; see interpretation above.

MeanInfit, MeanOutfit

Unweighted means of available level-specific mean squares, not pooled response-level Infit/Outfit.

MinEstimate, MaxEstimate

Native-scale measure range, omitting missing values but retaining infinite estimates.

The category_stats data.frame contains:

Category

Score category value.

Count, Percent

Sum of response weights for the category and its percentage of total weight; raw counts with unit weights.

Infit, Outfit

Descriptive category residual mean squares.

InfitZSTD, OutfitZSTD

Unavailable (NA); conditioning on the observed category does not preserve a universal unit-residual reference.

ExpectedCount, DiffCount, LowCount

Plug-in expected weighted count, observed minus expected count, and Count < 10 review flag. This cutoff is not a universal minimum independent sample size.

See also

diagnose_mfrm(), rating_scale_table(), describe_mfrm_data(), mfrmr_visual_diagnostics

Examples

# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("measurable_summary_table", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Saved synthetic JML/RSM analysis of example_core.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "core-jml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit
t5 <- measurable_summary_table(fit)
summary(t5)
p_t5 <- plot(t5, draw = FALSE)
plot_data(p_t5, "plot")
} # }
